reasons: These tests were not run during this review.
The prescription path has no test.
Tests check the output only, not the error handling.

terms.meaning: a Python tool that runs test functions and reports results
a check that must be true or the test fails
an old bug that comes back after a change

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Loads the test runner and the module being tested, including the unit table.
sections.why: Needed so the tests can call the code under test.
sections.watch_out: The unit table is imported but never used in this file.

sections.name: test_normalize_common_unit_mappings
sections.title: Standard unit fix tests
sections.what: Checks that each common misread unit in the table is corrected to its proper form.
sections.why: Protects the most frequent fixes from being broken.
sections.watch_out: Only a sample of table entries is checked.

sections.name: test_normalize_unit_regex_fallbacks
sections.title: Pattern rule tests
sections.what: Checks that misreads not in the table are rebuilt with a slash by the pattern rules, for mg, ng and pg units.
sections.why: Covers misreads that the table does not list.
sections.watch_out: Only three unit families are covered by these checks.

sections.name: test_normalize_empty_or_clean_units
sections.title: Empty and already-correct unit tests
sections.what: Checks that blank, missing, correct, and percent-sign units come back unchanged.
sections.why: Ensures the cleanup does not damage good data.
sections.watch_out: Other symbols and unusual units are not covered.

sections.name: test_structure_lab_report_normalization
sections.title: Lab report building test
sections.what: Builds a lab report from two sample results and confirms each unit is corrected.
sections.why: Checks the full path from raw entities to the list the app uses.
sections.watch_out: The count and the other fields in the result are not checked.

summary: Automated checks that the unit cleanup and lab-report building in the OCR service return the expected answers.
purpose: Catches mistakes when someone edits the unit table or the cleanup rules.
why: Likely reason: unit fixes are easy to break by accident, so a list of known inputs and expected outputs guards them.
how: Each test calls the unit function with known misreads and checks the answer. The last test builds a lab report from two sample entries and checks both units.
inputs: Hardcoded sample unit strings and sample entity dictionaries.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test, shown by pytest.
risks: Only a small set of inputs is covered. The prescription path and the unknown-document path have no tests. The unit table import is not used.
debug: Run pytest on this folder with the OCR service folder on the Python path. A failing assertion names the input and the wrong output it produced.
